Reviewed transaction/thread/device/tenant/credential/generation affinity, unbounded subpools, dependency outage, retry storm, stale credentials, secret contamination, and surgical-robot authority hazards.

evidence: Checked disjoint pool states, hard-capacity accounting, one borrower per exclusive lease, sanitation before reuse, invalid-resource destruction, bounded acquisition, structured release, policy-based affinity/fairness, and deterministic drain/destruction.
invariant_checking.notes: Worked examples and answers preserve ownership and capacity rules under database, memory, process, transaction, tenant, device, and safety-critical scenarios.

evidence: Reviewed the transition-system induction argument line by line against serialization, reservation, authentic lease, reset-before-availability, and exactly-once destruction assumptions.
Confirmed the executable trace demonstrates only its listed one-thread observations.
proof_review.notes: Liveness is correctly separated from safety and depends on return, creation, wakeup, scheduling, and starvation assumptions.

evidence: Audited invariant, induction, proof sketch, proves, guarantee, utilization, fair, healthy, safe, hard limit, and conclusion language.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter labels the formal argument as a proof sketch and bounds queueing, sanitation, health, timing, and high-stakes conclusions to their evidence.

evidence: Exact capacity, reuse, clearing, eviction, and replacement outputs reproduced.
Load, contention, fleet dependency, database, device, timing, and clinical evidence remain prescribed future work.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production performance, database compatibility, medical safety, external practitioner, or academic review is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter treats Object Pool as ownership, lifecycle, sanitation, and admission control; distinguishes memory reuse from scarce resources; and relates mechanisms to alternatives and contraction criteria.

practitioner_review.notes: The material covers realistic acquisition deadlines, queue policies, resource poisoning, reset contracts, affinity, global budgets, retry storms, telemetry, generation rollover, and graceful drain.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter progresses from a compact set model through lifecycle and queueing mechanisms to a runnable trace, ten domain-diverse examples, and five exercises with complete design-level answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
